tasks.short: Coordinate writers and editors, resolve blockers, and balance editorial workloads.

steps.what: Check deadlines, assignments and reported blockers in the {PROJECT}.
Read draft comments and progress notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Draft comments and progress notes for active assignments.
loop.output: A coordination agenda with source links and explicitly reported blockers.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each item; editor checks ambiguous or sensitive items.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per batch; unresolved items remain linked for manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text comments describe dependencies that status fields do not capture.

steps.what: Discuss blockers, give feedback and agree workload changes with writers and editors.
Record agreed owners, deadlines and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Send reminders and request missing progress updates through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} to show deadlines, dependencies and reported capacity, with scheduled reminders through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. A bounded extraction loop prepares a source-linked agenda from the {DOCS}; the editor holds the conversation and records decisions once in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Status fields, draft comments and personal context sit apart. Software can route work but cannot resolve sensitive feedback or competing commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and notifications cover routine coordination. AI-assisted coding makes a small connector and bounded comment extractor cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching, trust, hidden workload and disagreement about quality remain human work. Poorly maintained status fields still create misleading views.
tasks.human_edge: The editor notices strain, gives useful feedback and negotiates priorities without reducing people to activity measures.
tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time collecting updates and more time coaching and resolving dependencies. Capacity becomes easier to rebalance within existing delegation; staffing and performance decision rights do not automatically expand.

reach.learn: Campaign dependencies, priority trade-offs and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Shared assignment views, structured decisions and scheduled reminders are feasible through configuration; local coverage varies.
The proposed extraction loop can assist agenda preparation, but its accuracy and time savings need local validation.

assumptions: The setting is a marketing editorial team coordinating staff writers, editors and occasional contributors.
Coordination decisions are entered as structured changes during the discussion, replacing later transcription.
The agenda uses declared work information, without employee scoring or private-message monitoring.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Employee consultation follows national rules.
Build ranges are working-day effort estimates for a pilot; access or consultation waiting time may extend the calendar.
unknowns: Whether the {PROJECT} holds reliable owners, deadlines and dependencies.
Whether contributors can maintain brief progress notes.
Which draft comments contain restricted employee or customer information.
Which access permissions and consultation requirements apply locally.
research_questions: Does source-linked agenda preparation reduce preparation time without omitting important blockers?
Can existing {PROJECT} configuration cover the workflow before a connector is built?
new_work: Review extracted agenda items and remove sensitive or misleading summaries.
Maintain status definitions, reminder schedules and notification recipients.
Handle stale records and connector failures.

tasks.short: Choose coverage topics, assign writers and issue clear editorial briefs.

steps.what: Collect topic requests and event suggestions from {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Read supporting material in the {DOCS} and identify the requested angle.

loop.input: Topic request, campaign brief and linked source packet.
loop.output: Coverage options stating audience, angle, deadline and missing information.
loop.check: Link each factual item to its source; label suggestions and missing information separately.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per request; unresolved ambiguity goes to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests express audiences and editorial angles in varied free text.

steps.what: Check writer availability, existing assignments and deadlines in the {PROJECT}.
Discuss the angle and choose a writer, scope and deadline.
Write the assignment brief in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved assignment decision, source packet and standard brief template.
loop.output: An assignment brief with audience, angle, scope, sources and acceptance criteria.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source links; editor approves scope and instructions before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing decisions return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: The editorial angle and acceptance criteria need tailored prose beyond fixed template fields.

steps.what: Record the assignment in the {PROJECT} and send the brief through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure a topic queue and capacity view in the {PROJECT}, using structured intake through the {WORKFLOW}. Bounded loops extract coverage options and draft briefs in the {DOCS}; the editor chooses the assignment and approves the brief before the {PROJECT} routes it to the writer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Topic requests lack consistent fields, and writer suitability depends on context. Brief preparation and assignment records are often duplicated across documents and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, templates and routing already handle the structured work. Small bounded loops can turn varied requests into reviewable options and briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a useful angle, balancing development opportunities and matching sensitive subjects to writers require editorial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The editor understands audience needs and writer strengths, and can explain why an assignment matters.
tasks.altitude: The editor spends more time shaping coverage and developing writers, with less brief administration. The editor can propose a recurring introductory explainer slot; budget and campaign approval remain with existing owners.

reach.task: Turn recurring customer questions into research-backed content briefs.
reach.learn: Research quality, audience segmentation and limits of customer evidence.

reach.task: Define an explainer's angle and acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Interview planning, narrative structure and realistic reporting scope.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, templates and assignment routing can handle administrative steps without autonomous assignment decisions.
A controlled professional-writing experiment found benefits from assisted drafting; it does not establish savings for editorial assignment work.

assumptions: The editor assigns marketing articles, customer stories and event coverage rather than operating a full newsroom.
A structured topic form replaces routine copying from messages; unusual requests can still be attached.
Availability uses declared commitments, without inferring employee performance.
Routing covers internal writers; external contributor commitments need separate authority.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Employee consultation follows national rules.
Build ranges cover a pilot; consultation and access waiting time may extend delivery.
unknowns: Whether writer availability and expertise are recorded reliably.
Whether the editor can assign work directly or needs a campaign owner's approval.
Whether first-time buyers are an underserved audience.
Which source materials can be processed by an approved model service.
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Do generated briefs reduce clarification exchanges while preserving editorial intent?
Which brief fields can be populated entirely through templates and structured intake?
new_work: Review extracted angles and generated acceptance criteria.
Maintain brief templates, topic categories and declared availability.
Resolve duplicate requests and unclear campaign priorities.
Check that assignment records and approved briefs remain consistent.

tasks.short: Monitor source coverage and direct writers toward missing evidence or overlooked topics.

steps.what: Read incoming press releases and source updates in {EMAIL}.
Scan licensed media-monitoring feeds in {OTHER} and relevant mentions in {SOCIAL}.

loop.input: Permitted feed items, social mentions and source inbox items after exact duplicate filtering.
loop.output: A topic-grouped source digest with dates, links and attributed claims.
loop.check: Retain original items; validate links and dates; editor samples classifications and checks priority items.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per scheduled batch; uncertain items enter an unclassified queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Topic relevance varies in wording and context; keywords alone miss useful material and admit irrelevant items.

steps.what: Compare source use with the source register and coverage log in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Ask writers about unlogged interviews, offline sources and reporting obstacles.
Choose which source gaps require follow-up and agree reporting priorities.
Record agreed source follow-ups in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects permitted items from {EMAIL}, {SOCIAL} and licensed media-monitoring feeds in {OTHER}. Deterministic matching and a bounded classification loop feed a {BI} source-coverage view, while the editor investigates gaps and records approved follow-ups in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources span inboxes, feeds and private conversations. A complete picture depends on licensing, shared identifiers and writers recording offline work.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed connectors, stable item identifiers and scheduled joins cover collection and coverage comparisons. A bounded classifier helps organise varied text without making source credibility decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Missing sources cannot be inferred reliably from available feeds. Independent corroboration, confidential contacts and deliberate source selection remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The editor distinguishes visibility from importance, challenges source bias and protects confidential relationships.
tasks.altitude: The editor can review source gaps during active reporting rather than after drafts arrive. Follow-up priorities become better informed, while publication and source-protection responsibilities remain with the editor.

reach.task: Assess emerging issues before preparing a response.
reach.learn: Issue escalation, source attribution and the difference between repeated claims and corroboration.

reach.task: Assess gaps in the evidence supporting audience insights.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, source independence and evidence quality.

evidence.claim: Coosto offers conversation and news-topic monitoring, supporting the feasibility of configured source monitoring.
Full Fact AI flags checkable claims and matches repeats; this supports claim triage, not automatic verification.
Joining registered sources to coverage records can expose recorded gaps, but cannot establish that all relevant sources were used.

assumptions: For this marketing role, news gathering means industry, customer, campaign and event coverage.
The current team uses a small {SPREADSHEET} to connect source records with assignments.
Only licensed or otherwise permitted material is collected; access rights do not automatically permit model processing.
Gap calculations use explicit source categories and identifiers rather than model-generated completeness scores.
Confidential source identities are excluded from the shared digest.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Marketing processing has no assumed journalistic exemption.
Build ranges cover pilot effort; licensing, access and consultation under national rules may extend delivery.
unknowns: Which monitoring feeds and reuse licences the team holds.
Whether the source register and coverage log exist and use consistent identifiers.
How writers record offline sources without exposing confidential contacts.
Whether relevant feed interfaces are accessible.
Which consultation and data-processing approvals are required locally.
research_questions: How often does classification miss relevant items compared with manual monitoring?
Which source-gap indicators lead to useful follow-up rather than extra alerts?
How much apparent corroboration comes from sources repeating the same original claim?
new_work: Review unclassified items and sample digest accuracy.
Maintain source categories, licences, connectors and retention settings.
Investigate missing feeds and stale coverage records.
Adjust alert thresholds when irrelevant items accumulate.

tasks.short: Check publication proofs, request corrections and approve the exact version for production.

steps.what: Open the submitted proof and approved copy from the {DOCS}.
Compare proof text with approved copy for omissions and unintended changes.
Check spelling, terminology and house-style rules against the style guide.
Inspect layout, captions, image placement, legal notices and visual hierarchy.
Send marked corrections to the desktop publisher through {EMAIL}.
Recheck the corrected proof and approve its release to production.

tasks.design: Configure proof versions, annotations and correction routing in the {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic text comparison and configured style checks prepare exception reports; the editor inspects the rendered proof and authorises production against its exact version, with approval invalidated by later changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proofs and approved copy often use different formats, making comparisons noisy. Email approvals can refer to an unclear version, while layout judgement resists simple rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Version controls, text extraction, comparison libraries and configurable style rules cover much of the preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort needed to connect these established components.
tasks.still_hard: Reading order, outlined text and complex layouts can defeat text extraction. Misleading image-caption combinations and subtle presentation problems still need visual inspection.
tasks.human_edge: The editor judges the complete reader experience and accepts responsibility for the version released.
tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time locating versions and comparing unchanged text, concentrating on differences and presentation. Final release responsibility and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare reliable publication proofs and resolve production defects.
reach.learn: Reading order, font embedding, image resolution and layout preflight.

reach.task: Maintain consistent terminology and house-style checks.
reach.learn: Rule exceptions, false-positive handling and version-specific correction records.

evidence.claim: LanguageTool checks Dutch spelling, grammar, punctuation and style, supporting configured proofreading assistance.
Acrolinx supports repeatable style-guide scoring and quality gates; this does not establish visual proof approval.
Deterministic text comparison and version-bound approval can reduce comparison work and ambiguous release records.

assumptions: The composing-room equivalent is an internal desktop publisher or design team producing marketing publications.
Most proofs contain extractable text; extraction failures are flagged for manual comparison.
Submitted annotations become the correction request without a separate transcription step.
Correction work by the desktop publisher sits outside these editor-time shares.
Source claims were checked upstream; proof comparison does not establish their truth.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Required disclosure or editorial-review treatment is checked before release.
Build ranges include access and rollout effort; national consultation requirements may extend delivery.
unknowns: Which proof formats and layout templates are used.
How often proofs contain scanned or outlined text.
Whether approved copy has stable section identifiers.
Who has authority to release material to production.
Whether current approval records identify an immutable proof version.
Which access and consultation requirements apply locally.
research_questions: Which proof formats produce reliable text differences without hiding omissions?
Can the existing {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} invalidate approval automatically when a proof changes?
new_work: Maintain style rules, term lists and justified exceptions.
Handle extraction failures and noisy text comparisons.
Check that correction requests and approvals reference the intended proof version.
Review workflow failures before production deadlines.

role.altitude: The editor's week shifts from collecting updates, transcribing briefs and comparing versions toward coaching, audience choices, source quality and final presentation. Existing editorial authority becomes easier to exercise; broader budget, staffing or publication rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Marketing manager: rebalance campaign commitments using editorial capacity and dependencies.
Market research analyst: turn audience evidence and unanswered questions into useful coverage.
Public relations specialist: assess emerging issues and source credibility.
Desktop publisher: connect editorial approval with reliable production versions.
skills_to_grow: Structured editorial briefs and acceptance criteria.
Source provenance, corroboration and evidence gaps.
Configuring workflows, exception queues and style rules.
Evaluating bounded model outputs against original material.
Version control, proof comparison and production preflight.
Privacy-aware handling of contributor, employee and source information.
role.ambitious_version: An editor who runs a responsive audience-led publication programme, spots source gaps during reporting, develops writers and commissions introductory explainers for first-time buyers. Routine administration runs through configured systems, while editorial judgement and release accountability remain explicit.
